regions.shortDescription: A line chart with "efSearch, increasing" on the x-axis and no labeled y-axis. A solid blue curve labeled "Recall" rises steeply then flattens, showing diminishing returns. A dashed black line labeled "Latency" rises more steadily. A green dot marks "the knee: ~95–99% recall" near the point where the recall curve begins to flatten.
regions.plainLanguage: A chart showing that as efSearch increases, recall improves quickly at first then levels off, while latency keeps rising. A green dot marks the sweet spot at roughly 95–99% recall.

regions.shortDescription: A numbered list headed "What to remember" with four items: 01 HNSW is a skip list generalized to a proximity graph: coarse layers travel far, layer 0 refines. 02 Search is greedy descent from a single entry point — ~O(log N) hops, no training step. 03 The hierarchy comes from a random level draw at insert time; M links bound every node's degree. 04 In production, efSearch is your dial: sweep it, plot this curve, pick your (text appears cut off).
regions.plainLanguage: A four-point summary: HNSW uses layered graphs, search takes about O(log N) steps, node levels are assigned randomly at insert time, and efSearch lets you trade speed for recall in production.
